what: near duplicates at the write gate: the probe that must produce the failure first (ADR-007, amendment of 2026-10-13, evening; validated 2026-10-14, 11:05; built 2026-10-14, 12:35; run by the founder 2026-10-14, 13:00 to 14:16; read cold 14:30 from the sixteen files by near_duplicate_reading.read_near_duplicates(**load_from_dir(...)) in the declared order: the exits, F1, F2, the letter)
commands: python -m cortex_c2b.near_duplicate_probe --cues --ckpt <ckpt> --config <config> --row45 metrics\mqar\<row 45 file> --out metrics\mqar  (per checkpoint)
python -m cortex_c2b.hm_lm --near-duplicate-probe <arm> --ckpt <ckpt> --journal runs\near-dup\<run id>-<arm>.jsonl --config <config> --out metrics\mqar  (per checkpoint and arm B0, E0d, E1, E2)
order_run: stage 1 (13:00 UTC+2), the three cues files (seed 2024, 7, 1337; 13:21 to 13:33), the twelve arms (2024 B0, E0d, E1, E2; 7 the same; 1337 the same; 13:35 to 14:16), one command at a time, no stop

F1.rule: at least one near duplicate of E1 or E2 refused with its partner as the nearest stored code, under at least one encoder

E1.direction: fewer own citations under the near duplicates

E2.direction: fewer own citations under the near duplicates

F2.resolution: under Holm over the two primary tests the smaller p must be at or under 0.025: the first rejection needs at least seven discordant pairs all one way (six give 0.03125), the second six once the first is rejected (0.03125 against 0.05); so a loss of six questions in four hundred on either kind is invisible to the family, and a single test at 0.05 would need six (five give 0.0625)

hash_note: sha256 of the file's bytes with CRLF normalised to LF, first sixteen hexadecimal characters (the committed form); the files are written in LF by the instruments
